description:
## Finding

Two functions in `pkix-path/src/lib.rs` exceed clippy's default 100-line threshold:

| Function | Lines | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `chain_walk<V: SignatureVerifier>` | 489 | pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1947 |
| `check_name_constraints` | 109 | pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2794 |

`chain_walk` is the RFC 5280 §6.1 state-machine driver — it carries the policy tree, name-constraints state, and per-cert validation in a single body. At 489 lines it's hard to navigate, hard to test in isolation, and hard to reason about which RFC 5280 step is which.

## Why this matters

This is the most security-critical function in the entire workspace. RFC 5280 §6.1 has clearly named substeps (§6.1.3 input checks, §6.1.4 wrap-up, §6.1.5 final wrap-up); a function that maps 1:1 to RFC steps would make the code easier to audit against the spec and easier to fuzz/test per step.

## Suggestion

Refactor `chain_walk` into named helpers per RFC 5280 §6.1 substep:

- `step_basic_processing` — §6.1.3
- `step_preparation_for_next` — §6.1.4
- `step_wrap_up` — §6.1.5
- carry `WorkingState { permitted_subtrees, excluded_subtrees, valid_policy_tree, ... }` between them

`check_name_constraints` (109 lines) is closer to the threshold; one extraction (e.g., separating SAN-iteration from subject-DN constraint checks) would put it under.

## Priority

P3 — readability/auditability of the workspace's most critical function. Not a correctness bug per se. Big refactor though, so worth scoping carefully before doing.
design:
## chain_walk / check_name_constraints decomposition design

Reality vs. bead: `chain_walk` is 806 lines today (2032–2837), not 489. `check_name_constraints` is 159 lines (2868–3026), not 109. No `#[allow]` — `clippy::too_many_lines` is default-allowed. Doc-comment 2017–2024 explicitly argues against decomposition; any refactor must retire that comment honestly.

## 1. RFC 5280 §6.1 substep map

- §6.1.2 init: lib.rs:2042–2111
- §6.1.3(a)(1) signature verify: 2130–2152
- §6.1.3(a)(2) DN linkage / SAN-identity exception: 2154–2166
- §6.1.3(a)(2) validity: 2168–2169
- Project max-validity: 2171–2191
- Project min-RSA-bits: 2193–2205
- §6.1.3(d) critical-ext guard: 2207–2208
- §6.1.3(d)+(e) policy-tree update: 2210–2308 (99 lines, dominant)
- §6.1.3(f) early policy violation: 2310–2314
- §6.1.3(b) NameConstraints check: 2322–2334
- Project leaf SAN/EKU/rfc822 (e2/e3/e4): 2336–2392
- §6.1.4(k) BC cA / NotCA: 2398–2412
- §6.1.4(n) keyCertSign: 2414–2425
- §6.1.4(m) pathLenConstraint: 2427–2438
- §6.1.4(a)+(b) PolicyMappings: 2440–2514 (75 lines)
- §6.1.4(h) counter decrement: 2516–2524
- §6.1.4(i)/(j) PC/InhibitAnyPolicy clamp: 2526–2548
- §6.1.4(g) NC state update: 2550–2657 (108 lines)
- §6.1.4(c)–(f) state propagation: 2660–2666
- §6.1.5(a)–(b) leaf finalisation: 2669–2698
- §6.1.5(g) intersect tree with user-initial-policy-set: 2700–2828 (129 lines)
- §6.1.5 final check: 2830–2834

## 2. Natural decomposition (post-refactor order, smallest first)

| # | Helper | Substeps | Lines | Risk | Vis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | enforce_signature_alg_allowlist | algo allowlist | ~7 | low | pub(crate) |
| H2 | check_max_validity | project max-validity | ~17 | low | pub(crate) |
| H3 | check_min_rsa_bits | project min-RSA | ~10 | low | pub(crate) |
| H4 | verify_cert_signature<V> | §6.1.3(a)(1) | ~17 | low | pub(crate) |
| H5 | check_issuer_linkage | §6.1.3(a)(2) DN linkage | ~7 | low | pub(crate) |
| H6 | enforce_leaf_profile | e2+e3+e4 | ~57 | low-med | pub(crate) |
| H7 | check_intermediate_basic_constraints | §6.1.4(k)+(m) | ~33 | medium | pub(crate) |
| H8 | apply_policy_mappings | §6.1.4(a)+(b) | ~75 | HIGH | pub(crate) |
| H9 | update_policy_tree_from_cert | §6.1.3(d)+(e) | ~99 | HIGH | pub(crate) |
| H10 | update_name_constraints_state | §6.1.4(g) | ~108 | HIGH | pub(crate) |
| H11 | finalise_policy_tree_with_user_set | §6.1.5(a)+(b)+(g) | ~160 | HIGH | pub(crate) |

## 3. check_name_constraints decomposition

- N1 check_subject_dn_against_subtrees: ~22 lines, low risk
- N2 check_san_against_subtrees: ~19 lines, low risk
- N3 check_email_in_dn_against_rfc822: ~72 lines, medium risk (precondition guard `has_rfc822_constraint` is non-obvious and load-bearing)

Outer fn becomes a 12-line driver: excluded-pass → permitted-pass → N3.

## 4. Refactor sequence

Independent (parallelisable): H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, N1, N2.
Sequenced after H4/H5: H6.
Sequenced (must land in order): H7 → H8 → H9 → H10 → H11. Each one touches a load-bearing state machine; spread across separate PRs to keep PKITS regressions attributable.
N3 lands independently.

## 5. PKITS coverage gaps (where regressions hide)

- PKITS §4.4 (revocation), §4.5 (self-issued certs) — NOT IMPORTED. §4.5 exercises is_self_issued_cert exemptions in §6.1.3(b), §6.1.4(h), §6.1.4(m). H7, H10, H11 all touch self-issued logic; refactor regression there NOT caught by current tests.
- PKITS §4.16 (private cert extensions) — not imported.
- 8-way `initial_*` flag matrix in §6.1.5(g) — partial coverage; H11 is where this would bite.
- PolicyMappings + anyPolicy parents when policy_mapping==0 — exercised by ≤2 tests; risky for H8.
- NC empty-intersection via nc_constrained_types — DN/RFC822/DNS/URI tested; IPAddress and OtherName thin.

Single largest blind spot: self-issued + policy mapping + intersection emptying (H8/H10).

## 6. Recommended initial-PR scope

Land H1+H2+H3+H4+H5+N1+N2 in one PR. All low-risk, all pure-helper extractions, no policy/NC state-machine touch. Lines extracted: 58 from chain_walk, 41 from check_name_constraints.

Post-refactor: chain_walk ≈ 760 lines (still over 100), check_name_constraints ≈ 124 (still over).

**Honest conclusion: the low-risk scope does NOT bring chain_walk under 100 lines.** Three-PR plan:

1. PR-1: H1–H5 + N1–N2. Establishes helper pattern; no policy-tree risk. Add `#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]` with comment pointing at follow-up bead.
2. PR-2: H7 + H9 individually.
3. PR-3: H8 + H10 + H11.

Refusing to authorise a single-PR sub-100-line refactor is the correct call given current PKITS coverage.

## 7. Risks and concerns

- Author's monolith comment (2017–2024) is correct in spirit. Reviewers must verify each helper preserves the "tree becomes NULL when no nodes at depth ≥ 1" check (currently 3 identical sites: 2300–2303, 2509–2514, 2823–2826).
- nc_constrained_types invariant (2067–2072): bits are ORed in, never cleared. H10 must preserve this. NO test fails if a helper clears a bit — type-bit accounting is an internal invariant, not PKITS-checked. HIGH CONCERN.
- §6.1.4(h) counter-decrement ordering (2516–2524): must be after mappings (§6.1.4(b)), before clamps (§6.1.4(i)/(j)). If H8+H9 both extracted, call-order in chain_walk becomes load-bearing audit point. Must be commented at call site after refactor.
- working_issuer_is_san_identity propagation (line 2666): set after each iteration. If H5 extracts the linkage check but the assignment moves, SAN-identity exception (§4.2.1.6) breaks silently for chains where issuer (not leaf) uses SAN. PKITS does not test this. MEDIUM CONCERN. Keep assignment in chain_walk, not inside H5.
- prune_policy_tree (line 1145) has 3 call sites (2298, 2504, 2819) with matching "tree is NULL" checks → candidate for a small policy_tree_post_op_prune helper as a no-risk side improvement.
- §6.1.5(a) skips the RFC-mandated decrements of inhibit_any and policy_mapping with comment "neither is read after §6.1.5(a)" (lines 2683–2685). Static-analysis claim, not tested invariant. If H11 is extracted, comment must move with it; if any future code reads those after H11, the optimisation becomes a bug. Document at helper boundary.
- PKITS §4.5 (self-issued) coverage gap is the single largest unmonitored regression class. Recommend filing a separate bead to import PKITS §4.5 fixtures BEFORE H7/H10/H11 land, not after.
notes:
Decomposed into 17 child beads (PKIX-als9.1 through PKIX-als9.17) on 2026-05-08. See child list under CHILDREN.

Structure follows the design Section 4 sequencing:
- Independent / parallelisable: prep2, prep3, H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, N1, N2 (9 beads)
- After H4+H5: H6
- After H7 (start of high-risk chain): H7 → H8 → H9 → H10 → H11 (5 beads, sequenced)
- prep2 (WorkingState struct) gates H8
- N3 independent
- cleanup gates on H11 + N3, removes any clippy allow-attr added during refactor

Tooling note: 'bd ready' (strict) does not surface children due to the --parent relation creating an implicit parent-child dep that beads treats as a blocker. Use 'bd list --ready' (permissive) to see claimable children, or claim them directly with 'bd update PKIX-als9.<n> --claim'. The parent → child explicit deps correctly gate epic close (parent will close only when all 17 children close).
title: P3: chain_walk (489 lines) and check_name_constraints (109 lines) exceed clippy 100-line threshold; chain_walk is the RFC 5280 §6.1 driver
